proof_summary: The proof’s central invariant is that, for \(t\ge1\), a cell at \((t,x)\) is zero exactly when \(x=t-2v\) for some \(v\) with \(\binom{t-1}{v}\) odd; this is propagated through Rule 167 using Pascal’s identity and parity. At \(x=0\), a Lucas-theorem parity argument shows this occurs exactly when \(t\) is a power of two, equivalently \(t\mid2^{t+1}\), and appending the resulting center bit to the binary prefix gives the recurrence.
